raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Mamba radix checkpoints currently donate a GPU slot for every matched prefix. On a Kimi-K3 c=48 recipe that slot floor is `max_running_requests * 5` (480), so the GPU mamba pool stays large even when ReplaySSM already covers live verify and the checkpoint itself only needs to be reloaded from host.

## Modifications

Add `--enable-mamba-host-only-checkpoint` (default off). The flag requires `--enable-hierarchical-cache` and rejects `--enable-int8-mamba-checkpoint`.

When it is on:

- A finished request copies its flushed state into the hicache host pool and does not keep or donate a GPU slot.
- The mamba ratio drops to the live request plus ping-pong tracking slots. With the extra buffer and overlap that is 3 (1 active + 2 ping-pong), so a 96-wide decode pool is 288 slots. `no_buffer` with page size 1 is the path that returns 1.
- The Rust insert accepts `mamba_host_value` without a donated `mamba_value`.
- Under HiCache, a host checkpoint still counts as a device-prefix match, so the Full KV indices of that node stay reachable. Load-back still runs when the host hit length is non-zero.

The flag-off path is unchanged: the same ratio, the same donated GPU slot, and a host-only node does not advance `last_device_node`.

## Accuracy Tests

- `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_mamba_donated_alloc_ratio.py`: host-only ratio is 1 / 2 / 3 for no-buffer, lazy, and overlap. Flag-off cases stay at the previous ratios.
- `sglang-radix-tree` mamba component tests, including host-only insert with no GPU slot and the HiCache device-prefix match.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not in this PR. A c=48 AgentX run with the flag, `max-mamba-cache-size 288`, and `mem-fraction-static 0.87` is in progress separately.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.
